positions.thesis: Oracle is recovering strongly from a deep discount with excellent recent momentum. The 47% discount from highs indicates substantial bad news is priced in, while the 19% monthly gain signals the recovery is real.
evidence: It is about 47% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
The shares are up 19% over the past year and up 19% over the past month
positions.counterargument: The stock could have fallen for fundamental reasons that continue to deteriorate, and recent momentum may not reflect improving business conditions.

positions.thesis: Microsoft shows excellent recovery momentum despite flat annual performance. The recent 12% monthly gain after being 23% off highs suggests confidence in the business.
evidence: The shares are down 2% over the past year and up 12% over the past month
It is about 23% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: The YTD decline despite recent strength could mean the fundamental issues haven't been resolved and this is just a temporary bounce.

positions.thesis: Adobe has suffered significant losses but is bouncing back. The 40% discount and recent recovery signal genuine turnaround potential.
evidence: The shares are down 33% over the past year and up 4% over the past month
It is about 40% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: A 33% annual decline suggests serious business problems that a small monthly bounce may not resolve.

positions.thesis: Meta is stabilizing after weakness, trading well below its highs with modest strength returning. This defensive tech position offers downside protection.
evidence: The shares are up 7% over the past year and up 5% over the past month
It is about 23% below its high of the past year, so some bad news is already reflected in the price
positions.counterargument: Single-digit annual returns and only 5% monthly gains suggest business momentum remains weak despite recovery.

positions.thesis: Amazon combines strong annual growth with exceptional recent momentum, indicating robust business health and consumer demand.
evidence: The shares are up 41% over the past year and up 27% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Trading near all-time highs means little bad news is reflected in the price, creating downside risk if business slows.

positions.thesis: Apple offers quality tech exposure with strong growth momentum. As a leading company, it provides confidence for a nervous investor.
evidence: The shares are up 32% over the past year and up 10% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Trading close to highs leaves limited margin of safety and vulnerability to disappointing earnings.

positions.thesis: JPMorgan shows strong financial sector performance with consistent monthly gains. Financial leaders offer stability.
evidence: The shares are up 29% over the past year and up 6% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Financial sector could face headwinds from interest rate changes or economic slowdown.

positions.thesis: NVIDIA captures the AI trend with 78% annual gains. Recent monthly strength confirms continuing investor enthusiasm.
evidence: The shares are up 78% over the past year and up 13% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Massive gains mean valuation is stretched and susceptible to any disappointment in AI hype.

positions.thesis: Alphabet shows exceptional growth with 30% monthly momentum, representing a quality growth position despite valuation concerns.
evidence: The shares are up 140% over the past year and up 30% over the past month
positions.counterargument: The massive 140% gain and trading near highs means very little bad news is priced in, creating significant downside risk.

positions.thesis: American Express shows steady financial strength with consistent double-digit growth and monthly gains.
evidence: The shares are up 20% over the past year and up 6% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Financial sector valuations may be stretched if interest rates fall.

positions.thesis: Berkshire Hathaway offers defensive positioning and stability for a nervous investor despite slight underperformance.
evidence: The shares are down 11% over the past year and down 1% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Underperformance suggests the market sees better opportunities, and this position may continue to lag.

positions.thesis: Walmart combines consumer strength with consistent growth. Strong recent momentum supports position.
evidence: The shares are up 36% over the past year and up 6% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Trading near highs creates vulnerability if consumer spending slows.

positions.thesis: Coca-Cola provides defensive consumer staples exposure with modest consistent gains.
evidence: The shares are up 13% over the past year and up 3% over the past month
positions.counterargument: Slow growth rate offers limited upside potential.

reasoning: As a nervous retail investor with limited experience, I built this portfolio around two core principles: buying stocks that have already had bad news reflected in their prices (discounts from highs) combined with demonstrating recovery momentum, while keeping over half in cash for safety and flexibility. I emphasized financial and technology leaders with authoritative track records, avoided extreme outliers with suspicious gains, and excluded stocks showing recent monthly weakness despite annual strength, as these signal potential problems.
